title: Avianca 4
summary: Avianca Flight 4, a Douglas C-54, stalled shortly after takeoff from Cartagena, Colombia. The aircraft reached only 70 feet altitude before beginning to descend and crashed into shallow water just 1,300 meters from the runway, killing 56 of 64 aboard. Investigation found engine failure was possible but unproven; poor maintenance practices and inadequate inspections were also suspected.
probable_cause: Engine failure suspected but not definitively proven. Contributing factors included poor maintenance practices and inadequate inspection program that may have allowed undetected defects to develop.

title: Britannia Airways 105
summary: Britannia Airways Flight 105, a Bristol Britannia 102 operating from London Luton to Ljubljana, Yugoslavia, crashed during final approach on September 1, 1966. The aircraft struck trees in woods near Nasovče, approximately 2.8 kilometers from the runway threshold and below the approach path. Subsequent investigation determined that the pilot-in-command had set his altimeter to the wrong pressure setting. The difference between the required QFE setting (968 millibars) and what was set (1005.5 or higher) resulted in the aircraft being approximately 1,100 feet lower than the prescribed safe altitude during approach. Neither pilot detected this altimeter error during approach, and no cross-check was performed despite procedural requirements. The crew relied on visual approach in moonlit night conditions over forested terrain without distinguishing visual landmarks. All 98 of 117 passengers and crew were killed in the crash.
probable_cause: Altimeter setting error by pilot-in-command who failed to set barometric pressure to QFE value provided by air traffic control, resulting in aircraft descending 1,100 feet below procedurally safe altitudes. Contributing factors included failure of pilot monitoring to detect the altimeter error through cross-check, failure to follow published approach procedures, and visual illusion from false altitude perception.

title: 1966 Flying Tiger Line Canadair CL-44 crash
summary: A Flying Tiger Line Canadair CL-44 operating from Tachikawa Air Force Base in Japan to Da Nang, South Vietnam on December 24, 1966, crashed while on final approach to Da Nang Airport. The aircraft approached in rain and foggy conditions with fuel tanks running near empty, making an abort of the landing approach impossible. A kilometer south of the runway, the aircraft clipped trees and crashed into Binh Thai village, plowing through 55 thatched huts over 275 meters. All four crew members were killed, along with 107 people on the ground. This was the first and deadliest accident for the Canadair CL-44 aircraft type.
probable_cause: Controlled flight into terrain during approach in poor weather conditions, with the aircraft descending below the glide path during the approach phase, resulting from crew continuing descent in reduced visibility rather than executing go-around.
